description: Full-polish rewrite of the Wear OS sign-in screen: replace invisible BasicTextField inputs with tappable RemoteInput chips, add validation, phone fallback, and post-failure UX.

userStories.title: Add Wear OS input/remote-interactions dependencies
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the Wear OS input and remote-interactions libraries available so RemoteInputIntentHelper and RemoteActivityHelper can be used in the sign-in screen.
acceptanceCriteria: gradle/libs.versions.toml defines wearInput = "1.4.0" under [versions] and androidx-wear-input = { group = "androidx.wear", name = "wear-input", version.ref = "wearInput" } under [libraries]

gradle/libs.versions.toml defines wearRemoteInteractions = "1.1.0" under [versions] and androidx-wear-remote-interactions = { group = "androidx.wear", name = "wear-remote-interactions", version.ref = "wearRemoteInteractions" } under [libraries]
wear/build.gradle.kts implementation dependencies include libs.androidx.wear.input and libs.androidx.wear.remote.interactions
./gradlew :wear:assembleDebug completes without error
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Check https://maven.google.com for the latest stable versions of wear-input and wear-remote-interactions before hardcoding versions. Both are Wear OS specific — add only to the :wear module.

userStories.title: Replace BasicTextField inputs with RemoteInput chips
userStories.description: As a user, I want to tap a visible chip to enter my email and password so that the system keyboard dialog opens and I can actually type on my watch.
acceptanceCriteria: All BasicTextField usages are removed from SignInScreen.kt

Email and password are each represented by an OutlinedButton (full width) showing placeholder text when empty or the entered value when filled; the password chip shows bullet characters (•••) instead of the raw value

Tapping the email chip builds a RemoteInput with key 'email_input' and label 'Enter email', constructs an intent via RemoteInputIntentHelper.createActionRemoteInputIntent() with that RemoteInput, and launches it via rememberLauncherForActivityResult(ActivityResultContracts.StartActivityForResult())
Tapping the password chip builds a RemoteInput with key 'password_input' and label 'Enter password', and launches it the same way; the password chip never pre-populates with a previous value
The activity result callback extracts the string via RemoteInput.getResultsFromIntent(result.data)?.getString(key) and stores it in the ViewModel via onEmailChange / onPasswordChange callbacks
SignInViewModel stores email and password as MutableStateFlow<String> fields (initialized to "") and exposes them as StateFlow; SignInScreen.kt observes them to display current chip values
SignInScreenContent parameter list is updated to accept emailValue: String and passwordValue: String
./gradlew :wear:assembleDebug completes without error
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001. androidx.core.app.RemoteInput is in core-ktx; for Wear OS intent wiring use androidx.wear.input.RemoteInputIntentHelper. The launcher must be created with rememberLauncherForActivityResult at the composable call site, not inside a click handler.

userStories.title: Add client-side validation before sign-in
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see an immediate inline error if I tap Sign In with blank or malformed fields so that I am not waiting on a network round-trip for an avoidable error.
acceptanceCriteria: If email is blank when Sign In is tapped, a Text 'Email is required' appears below the email chip in MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error color; viewModel.signIn() is NOT called
If password is blank when Sign In is tapped, a Text 'Password is required' appears below the password chip in MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error color; viewModel.signIn() is NOT called
If email does not contain '@', a Text 'Enter a valid email address' appears below the email chip in error color; viewModel.signIn() is NOT called
Validation errors are stored as emailError: String? and passwordError: String? in SignInViewModel and exposed as StateFlow
Tapping the email chip clears emailError; tapping the password chip clears passwordError
When all fields are valid, viewModel.signIn() is called normally and no validation error Text items are visible
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-002. Validation runs inside the onSignIn lambda in SignInScreen before delegating to the ViewModel. Keep validation logic in the ViewModel (validate() method) so it is testable. Email regex: just check contains('@') — full RFC validation is overkill here.

userStories.title: Post-failure UX: clear password and highlight error chip
userStories.description: As a user, I want the password chip to clear and turn red after a failed sign-in so that I know exactly which field to correct without reading a wall of text.
acceptanceCriteria: In SignInViewModel, when ClerkResult.Failure is received in signIn(), the password StateFlow is reset to ""
When SignInUiState is Error, the password chip's container color is set to MaterialTheme.colorScheme.errorContainer and its content color to MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onErrorContainer
When SignInUiState is Error, the existing error Text from the Clerk failure message remains visible below the password chip
Tapping the password chip to re-enter (i.e. when a new password_input result arrives) transitions UiState back to Idle, clears the error message, and resets the chip color to its default
The email chip is NOT highlighted or cleared on sign-in failure
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-002 and US-003. The chip color logic lives in SignInScreenContent: derive chip colors from a when(uiState) expression — use ButtonDefaults.outlinedButtonColors() for Idle/Loading, and a copy with errorContainer for Error state.

userStories.title: Add 'Use phone' fallback button
userStories.description: As a user whose watch keyboard is unavailable, I want a secondary button that opens sign-in on my paired phone so that I am not blocked.
acceptanceCriteria: A CompactButton labelled 'Use phone' is rendered below the Sign In button in SignInScreenContent, styled as a secondary/outlined action
Tapping 'Use phone' calls RemoteActivityHelper(context).startRemoteActivity(Intent('com.pl.pulselab.SIGN_IN'), null) wrapped in a try/catch

If RemoteActivityHelper throws (no paired phone or phone app not installed), a Text 'Phone not available' is shown below the button in MaterialTheme.colorScheme.error color for 3 seconds then hidden (use a LaunchedEffect with delay(3000) to reset state)
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml registers an <intent-filter> for action 'com.pl.pulselab.SIGN_IN' on MainActivity (stub — no actual phone sign-in UI needed yet)
The 'Use phone' button is disabled (enabled = false) while SignInUiState is Loading
./gradlew :wear:assembleDebug and ./gradlew :app:assembleDebug both complete without error
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001 (wear-remote-interactions). RemoteActivityHelper requires a Context — obtain via LocalContext.current inside SignInScreenContent. The intent action string 'com.pl.pulselab.SIGN_IN' must match exactly between the wear launcher and the phone manifest filter.
